chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
A man drank wine during the time of Abū Bakr, so he was brought before Abū Bakr. He said to him, “Did you drink wine?” He said, “Yes.” He said, “And why, when it is forbidden?”

He said: The man said to him, “I accepted Islam, and my Islam became good, and my dwelling is among a people who drink wine and deem it permissible. Had I known that it was forbidden, I would have avoided it.” Then Abū Bakr turned to ʿUmar and said, “What do you say regarding the matter of this man?” ʿUmar said, “It is a difficult problem, and none is fit for it except Abū al-Ḥasan.” He said, “Call ʿAlī for us.” ʿUmar said, “The judge is to be approached in his house.” So they rose, with the man accompanying them, along with those of the people who were present with them, until they came to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام. They informed him of the man’s story, and the man himself related his account.

He said: Then he said, “Send with him someone who will take him around to the gatherings of the Muhājirīn and the Anṣār. Whoever had recited to him the verse of prohibition, let him testify against him.” So they did that, but no one testified against him that he had recited to him the verse of prohibition. So he let him go and said to him, “If you drink after this, we will carry out the hadd punishment upon you.”

key_terms.آيَةَ التَّحْرِيمِ: the verse of prohibition; the revealed Quranic ruling forbidding wine
key_terms.الْأَنْصَارِ: the Helpers; the Muslims of Madinah who supported the Emigrants
key_terms.الْمُهَاجِرِينَ: the Emigrants; the early Muslims who migrated from Makkah
key_terms.خَمْرًا: wine; the intoxicating drink at issue in the case
key_terms.مُعْضِلَةٌ: a difficult legal problem requiring expert judgment

ai.seo_question: Can the hadd punishment for drinking wine be applied if a person was unaware of its prohibition?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates a legal case in which a man who had newly accepted Islam drank wine, claiming ignorance of its prohibition. Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī عليه السلام ordered that it be verified whether the ruling had actually reached him, and when no proof was found, he released him and warned that the hadd would apply thereafter. The report highlights the requirement of establishing knowledge before enforcing a legal punishment.
